strategies.title: Protective put
strategies.simple: Buy the stock and buy a put 7% below it: insurance that pays if the stock falls through the strike.
strategies.thesis: Bullish, but you want a floor under the position.
strategies.best_when: you expect gains but cannot afford a large drawdown (a review, a limit, a mandate).
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the fall to the strike plus the premium; upside unlimited less the premium.
strategies.notes: Closer strikes protect more and cost more: 1–2% below is strong, 7% moderate, 15% cheap crash insurance.

strategies.title: Protective put, tight (2% below)
strategies.simple: Buy the stock and a put just 2% below it: strong protection at a high price.
strategies.thesis: You want almost no downside and will pay for it.
strategies.best_when: an event is close (earnings, a decision) and the stock is a large part of the book.
strategies.risk: Loss capped near 2% plus a large premium; the premium is the cost of sleeping.

strategies.title: Protective put, at the money
strategies.simple: Buy the stock and a put right at the market.
strategies.thesis: Full protection from today's price.
strategies.best_when: you must hold the stock but want none of the downside for a while.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the premium; the stock must rise more than the premium before you profit.

strategies.title: Tail-risk hedge (17% below)
strategies.simple: Buy the stock and a put far below it: cheap insurance against a crash only.
strategies.thesis: Normal declines are acceptable; a catastrophe is not.
strategies.best_when: a long-term holding in a fragile market; the premium must stay small.
strategies.risk: You absorb the first ~17% of any fall; the put only helps beyond it.

strategies.title: Collar
strategies.simple: Buy the stock, buy a put below, sell a call above: protection paid for by giving up upside beyond the call.
strategies.thesis: Bullish inside a band; you accept a cap to make the floor cheaper.
strategies.best_when: you want to hold through a risky period at little cost.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the put strike; gains capped at the call strike; net premium small either way.

strategies.title: Zero-cost collar
strategies.simple: A collar whose sold call pays exactly for the bought put.
strategies.thesis: Free protection in exchange for a cap.
strategies.best_when: you refuse to pay premium and can live with limited upside.
strategies.risk: Same as a collar: floor at the put, ceiling at the call, no cash today.

strategies.title: Put-spread hedge
strategies.simple: Buy the stock, buy a put below and sell one farther below: cheaper protection that stops at the lower strike.
strategies.thesis: You want protection against a moderate fall, not a total collapse.
strategies.best_when: puts are expensive (high implied vol) and you expect a 5–15% correction at worst.
strategies.risk: Protected only between the two strikes; below the lower one you lose again.

strategies.title: Put-spread collar
strategies.simple: Stock, a put spread below and a short call above: a collar with cheaper, capped protection.
strategies.thesis: Trade some crash protection for a higher call strike.
strategies.best_when: you want more upside than a plain collar allows.
strategies.risk: Protection stops at the lower put; upside capped at the call.

strategies.title: Long stock + call (extra upside)
strategies.simple: Buy the stock and a call above it: more exposure if it rallies.
strategies.thesis: Very bullish: leverage the upside.
strategies.best_when: you expect a sharp move up soon.
strategies.risk: Full stock downside plus the premium; not a hedge.

strategies.title: Long stock + temporary futures hedge
strategies.simple: Keep the stock and short index futures for a while: market risk off, stock-specific risk on.
strategies.thesis: Long-term bullish, short-term worried about the market.
strategies.best_when: you want to keep the position (tax, mandate) but cut beta for a month.
strategies.risk: You still lose if the stock underperforms the index; you miss a market rally while hedged.

strategies.title: Protected short
strategies.simple: Short the stock and buy a call 10% above it: the call caps the loss if the stock rallies.
strategies.thesis: Bearish, with a ceiling on the pain.
strategies.best_when: shorting a name that could squeeze.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the rise to the call strike plus premium; profit is the fall less the premium.

strategies.title: Strongly protected short
strategies.simple: Short the stock and buy a call just 2% above it.
strategies.thesis: Bearish with tight protection.
strategies.best_when: an event could gap the stock up.
strategies.risk: Loss capped near 2% plus a large premium.

strategies.title: Short catastrophe hedge
strategies.simple: Short the stock and buy a call 20% above it: cheap protection against a monster rally only.
strategies.thesis: Bearish; only a squeeze would hurt.
strategies.best_when: the borrow is cheap and a takeover is the only real risk.
strategies.risk: You absorb the first ~20% rally.

strategies.title: Short collar
strategies.simple: Short the stock, buy a call above, sell a put below: protection paid for by giving up profit below the put.
strategies.thesis: Bearish inside a band.
strategies.best_when: you expect a moderate fall and want cheap protection.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the call strike; profit capped at the put strike.

strategies.title: Call-spread hedge for a short
strategies.simple: Short the stock; buy a call above and sell one farther above: cheaper protection that stops at the higher strike.
strategies.thesis: Protect against a moderate rally, not a moonshot.
strategies.best_when: calls are expensive and a huge squeeze is unlikely.
strategies.risk: Protection only between the strikes.

strategies.title: Short stock + put (extra downside)
strategies.simple: Short the stock and buy a put below it: more exposure if it falls.
strategies.thesis: Very bearish.
strategies.best_when: you expect a sharp move down soon.
strategies.risk: Full short-squeeze risk plus the premium; not a hedge.

strategies.title: Long call
strategies.simple: Buy a call: the right to buy the stock at the strike. Profit if it rallies past the strike plus premium.
strategies.thesis: Bullish with a known maximum loss.
strategies.best_when: you want upside without funding the shares, and expect a move before expiry.
strategies.risk: Lose the premium if the stock stays below the strike; time decay works against you.

strategies.title: Long put
strategies.simple: Buy a put: the right to sell at the strike. Profit if the stock falls below the strike minus premium.
strategies.thesis: Bearish with a known maximum loss.
strategies.best_when: you expect a fall and do not want the borrow of a short.
strategies.risk: Lose the premium if the stock stays above the strike.

strategies.title: Synthetic long (call + short put)
strategies.simple: Buy a call and sell a put at the same strike: behaves like owning the stock, for little cash.
strategies.thesis: Long exposure with margin instead of capital.
strategies.best_when: you want stock-like exposure without the shares.
strategies.risk: Same as long stock: unlimited downside below the strike.

strategies.title: Synthetic short (put + short call)
strategies.simple: Buy a put and sell a call at the same strike: behaves like a short, without borrowing.
strategies.thesis: Short exposure without a locate.
strategies.best_when: the stock is hard to borrow.
strategies.risk: Same as a short: unlimited loss on a rally.

strategies.title: Risk reversal (bullish)
strategies.simple: Sell a put below and buy a call above: cheap or free bullish exposure with downside if the stock falls.
strategies.thesis: Bullish; the put you sell pays for the call.
strategies.best_when: puts are dear relative to calls (skew is steep).
strategies.risk: Below the put strike you own the stock, effectively; above the call you profit.

strategies.title: Covered call
strategies.simple: Own the stock and sell a call 10% above it: collect the premium; above the strike you give up the gain.
strategies.thesis: Moderately bullish or flat: harvest premium.
strategies.best_when: implied vol is high and you would be happy to sell at the strike.
strategies.risk: Not a downside hedge: you keep the full fall, less the premium.

strategies.title: Partial covered call
strategies.simple: Own the stock and write calls on only half of it.
strategies.thesis: Some premium, some uncapped upside.
strategies.best_when: you like the stock but want a little income.
strategies.risk: Half the position is capped; the whole position keeps the downside.

strategies.title: Cash-secured put
strategies.simple: Sell a put below the market with cash set aside: get paid to wait to buy the stock lower.
strategies.thesis: You would own the stock, but only cheaper.
strategies.best_when: you want to buy on a dip and vol is high.
strategies.risk: If it falls hard you buy at the strike and keep falling with it, less the premium.

strategies.title: Covered strangle
strategies.simple: Own the stock, sell a call above and a put below: double premium; you may be assigned more stock lower.
strategies.thesis: Range-bound stock you want more of if it dips.
strategies.best_when: high vol, a name you are happy to add to.
strategies.risk: Large exposure below the put (you would own twice as much); capped above the call.

strategies.title: Jade lizard
strategies.simple: Sell a put below and a call spread above: premium with no risk on the upside if the credit exceeds the call-spread width.
strategies.thesis: Neutral to bullish premium collection.
strategies.best_when: vol is rich and you do not fear a rally.
strategies.risk: Downside like a short put; the upside risk is bounded by the spread width less the credit.

strategies.title: Bull call spread
strategies.simple: Buy a call near the market and sell one farther above: cheaper than a call; profit capped at the higher strike.
strategies.thesis: Bullish to a target.
strategies.best_when: you expect a move up to a level, not beyond.
strategies.risk: Lose the net premium if the stock stays below the lower strike.

strategies.title: Bull put spread
strategies.simple: Sell a put below and buy one farther below: a credit if the stock stays up; the bought put caps the damage.
strategies.thesis: Bullish or neutral, paid to wait.
strategies.best_when: you expect support to hold.
strategies.risk: Max loss is the width between strikes less the credit.

strategies.title: Call ratio spread (1×2)
strategies.simple: Buy one call and sell two farther above: cheap or free upside to the short strike, danger beyond it.
strategies.thesis: Mildly bullish: a drift up, not a rocket.
strategies.best_when: you expect a grind higher and want it for free.
strategies.risk: Above the short strike losses grow without limit (naked call).

strategies.title: Bear put spread
strategies.simple: Buy a put near the market and sell one farther below: cheaper than a put; profit capped at the lower strike.
strategies.thesis: Bearish to a target.
strategies.best_when: you expect a fall to a level.
strategies.risk: Lose the net premium if the stock stays above the upper strike.

strategies.title: Bear call spread
strategies.simple: Sell a call above and buy one farther above: a credit if the stock stays below the sold strike.
strategies.thesis: Bearish or neutral, paid to wait.
strategies.best_when: you expect resistance to hold.
strategies.risk: Max loss is the width less the credit.

strategies.title: Long straddle
strategies.simple: Buy a call and a put at the money: profit from a big move either way.
strategies.thesis: A large move is coming; direction unknown.
strategies.best_when: before an event, when implied vol is still cheap.
strategies.risk: Both premiums decay if nothing happens; needs a move bigger than the combined premium.

strategies.title: Long strangle
strategies.simple: Buy a call above and a put below: a cheaper straddle that needs a bigger move.
strategies.thesis: Big move coming, cheaply.
strategies.best_when: same as the straddle with less premium at risk.
strategies.risk: Both premiums lost inside the strikes.

strategies.title: Short straddle
strategies.simple: Sell a call and a put at the money: collect a lot of premium; lose if the stock moves far either way.
strategies.thesis: Nothing will happen.
strategies.best_when: implied vol is far above realised and no event is due.
strategies.risk: Unlimited loss on a big move: a learning exercise best defined with wings (iron butterfly).

strategies.title: Short strangle
strategies.simple: Sell a call above and a put below: premium with a wider comfort zone than the straddle.
strategies.thesis: The stock stays in a range.
strategies.best_when: rich vol, quiet calendar.
strategies.risk: Unlimited beyond either strike.

strategies.title: Iron condor
strategies.simple: Sell a put and a call around the market, buy a put and a call farther out: premium with capped loss.
strategies.thesis: Range-bound, defined risk.
strategies.best_when: you want the short strangle's income with a known worst case.
strategies.risk: Max loss is the wing width less the credit, on either side.

strategies.title: Reverse iron condor
strategies.simple: Buy a put and a call near the market, sell one farther out on each side: a cheaper bet on a big move, capped.
strategies.thesis: A move is coming; you want it defined.
strategies.best_when: a strangle is too expensive.
strategies.risk: Lose the net premium if the stock stays in the middle; gains capped at the outer strikes.

strategies.title: Iron butterfly
strategies.simple: Sell a call and a put at the money, buy a call and a put farther out: a short straddle with wings.
strategies.thesis: The stock pins near today's price.
strategies.best_when: rich vol, a range you trust.
strategies.risk: Max loss is the wing width less the (large) credit.

strategies.title: Long call butterfly
strategies.simple: Buy one call below, sell two at the target, buy one above: a cheap bet that the stock lands near the middle strike.
strategies.thesis: A specific price target with small premium at risk.
strategies.best_when: you have a target and time.
strategies.risk: Lose the small debit outside the wings; max gain at the middle strike.

strategies.title: Broken-wing put butterfly
strategies.simple: A put butterfly with the far wing moved farther out: often a credit, with risk only on a large fall.
strategies.thesis: Mildly bearish to neutral, paid to enter.
strategies.best_when: you expect a drift down toward the middle strike.
strategies.risk: Beyond the far wing the loss equals the extra width less the credit.

strategies.title: Calendar spread
strategies.simple: Sell a near-dated call and buy a later-dated call at the same strike: profit from time decay on the short leg while the stock sits near the strike.
strategies.thesis: Quiet now, movement later.
strategies.best_when: near-term vol is rich versus later months.
strategies.risk: Lose the net debit if the stock runs far from the strike before the near expiry.

strategies.title: Poor man's covered call (diagonal)
strategies.simple: Buy a long-dated in-the-money call instead of the stock and sell short-dated calls against it.
strategies.thesis: A covered call with less capital.
strategies.best_when: you want covered-call income on a stock you cannot afford in size.
strategies.risk: The long call can lose most of its value if the stock falls; short calls cap the upside each cycle.

strategies.title: Put calendar
strategies.simple: Sell a near put and buy a later put at the same strike below the market: a cheap way to own longer-dated protection.
strategies.thesis: Protection later, financed by decay now.
strategies.best_when: you want a put for next quarter but not this month.
strategies.risk: A fast drop before the near expiry hurts; net debit at risk.

strategies.title: Synthetic long (receive TRS)
strategies.simple: Receive the stock's total return from a dealer in exchange for funding plus a spread: long without owning the shares.
strategies.thesis: Long exposure with financing built in.
strategies.best_when: you want leverage or cannot hold the shares directly.
strategies.risk: Full stock downside plus the spread; the dealer's credit.
strategies.reason: NOT ELIGIBLE / not a PB account (TRS legs deal through a prime broker in an eligible lifetime)

strategies.title: Synthetic short (pay TRS)
strategies.simple: Pay the stock's total return: short without borrowing the shares yourself.
strategies.thesis: Short exposure via a dealer.
strategies.best_when: the borrow is scarce or you want one line for a short.
strategies.risk: Unlimited on a rally, like any short; the dealer's credit.
strategies.reason: NOT ELIGIBLE / not a PB account (TRS legs deal through a prime broker in an eligible lifetime)

strategies.title: Protected synthetic long
strategies.simple: Receive the TRS and buy a put below: stock plus put, without the shares.
strategies.thesis: Leveraged long with a floor.
strategies.best_when: you want the synthetic long but with insurance.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the put strike plus premium and spread.
strategies.reason: NOT ELIGIBLE / not a PB account (TRS legs deal through a prime broker in an eligible lifetime)

strategies.title: Protected synthetic short
strategies.simple: Pay the TRS and buy a call above: short stock plus call, without the borrow.
strategies.thesis: Synthetic short with a ceiling on losses.
strategies.best_when: you short via swap and fear a squeeze.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the call strike.
strategies.reason: NOT ELIGIBLE / not a PB account (TRS legs deal through a prime broker in an eligible lifetime)

strategies.title: Long stock, protected, plus TRS overlay
strategies.simple: Own the stock with a put, and add extra bullish exposure through a received TRS.
strategies.thesis: Core position protected, extra conviction on top.
strategies.best_when: high conviction, limited cash.
strategies.risk: The overlay is unprotected: it carries full downside.
strategies.reason: NOT ELIGIBLE / not a PB account (TRS legs deal through a prime broker in an eligible lifetime)

strategies.title: Delta-neutral TRS (financing basis)
strategies.simple: Receive the TRS and short the same shares: direction cancels; what is left is financing and dividends.
strategies.thesis: Earn or pay the basis, not the direction.
strategies.best_when: you want to learn what a swap really costs.
strategies.risk: Small: spread, borrow cost and dividend timing.
strategies.reason: NOT ELIGIBLE / not a PB account (TRS legs deal through a prime broker in an eligible lifetime)

strategies.title: Bullish through futures
strategies.simple: Buy index futures: linear market exposure on margin, no strike, no premium.
strategies.thesis: Bullish on the market.
strategies.best_when: you want beta quickly and cheaply.
strategies.risk: Full downside, settled daily as variation margin.

strategies.title: Bearish through futures
strategies.simple: Sell index futures: linear short exposure on margin.
strategies.thesis: Bearish on the market.
strategies.best_when: you want to hedge a book or bet against the index.
strategies.risk: Unlimited on a rally, settled daily.

strategies.title: Long futures with crash protection
strategies.simple: Buy index futures and a put on the index below the level you can tolerate.
strategies.thesis: Leveraged long with a floor.
strategies.best_when: you want beta with insurance.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the put strike plus premium.

strategies.title: Short futures with rally protection
strategies.simple: Sell index futures and buy a call above.
strategies.thesis: Short beta with a ceiling.
strategies.best_when: hedging a book without unlimited squeeze risk.
strategies.risk: Loss limited to the call strike plus premium.

strategies.title: Beta-hedged long (stock vs index)
strategies.simple: Buy the stock and short index futures in notional: you keep only the stock's own performance.
strategies.thesis: The stock beats the market; the market itself is not the bet.
strategies.best_when: a stock-specific view in an uncertain market.
strategies.risk: You lose if the stock lags the index, whatever the index does.

strategies.title: Pair: long the other name, short this one
strategies.simple: Long the second name, short the underlying, same notional: profit from the spread between them, not the market.
strategies.thesis: The second name outperforms the first (QQQ vs SPY, MSFT vs SPY).
strategies.best_when: you have a relative view and want no beta.
strategies.risk: The spread can widen against you without limit; a short needs a borrow.

strategies.title: Pair: long this one, short the other name
strategies.simple: Long the underlying, short the second name.
strategies.thesis: The underlying outperforms the second name.
strategies.best_when: the opposite relative view.
strategies.risk: As above.

strategies.title: Protected single-stock pair
strategies.simple: Long the second name with a put on it, short the underlying for market beta.
strategies.thesis: A stock-specific long with company risk insured and market risk hedged.
strategies.best_when: the long is a single stock that could gap.
strategies.risk: Spread risk plus the premium.

strategies.title: Stock repair
strategies.simple: On a stock you own that has fallen: buy one call near the market and sell two above it, for about zero cost — you break even sooner, and give up gains above the short strike.
strategies.thesis: Get back to break-even faster on a loser.
strategies.best_when: you are underwater and expect a partial recovery, not a full rally.
strategies.risk: No extra downside; upside capped at the short strike (the second short call is covered by the stock).

strategies.title: Seagull (bullish)
strategies.simple: Buy a call spread and sell a put below: cheap or free upside to the call spread's top, with downside below the put.
strategies.thesis: Bullish to a target, financed by taking the downside.
strategies.best_when: you would buy the stock lower anyway.
strategies.risk: Below the put you are effectively long the stock; gains capped at the upper call.

strategies.title: Strap (bullish straddle)
strategies.simple: Buy two calls and one put at the money: a straddle that leans bullish.
strategies.thesis: Big move likely, more likely up.
strategies.best_when: an event with an upside skew of outcomes.
strategies.risk: All premiums lost if nothing moves.

note: 60 templates (finsim/engines/playbook.py); option-only templates fill all-or-none (AON), the others sequentially
